# The Setup Dialog Stops Blaming Your Router

The second pre-release for [#57](https://github.com/timmaurice/bergfex/issues/57). `3.2.0-beta.1` made a refused poll legible; this one does the same for the setup and reconfigure dialogs, which were the one place a blocked user could still be sent in the wrong direction.

## Fixes

- **A refusal no longer reads as "check your internet connection".** Adding a resort, or changing an entry's language, first asks bergfex whether the page serves. Every failure collapsed into `cannot_connect` — *"Failed to connect to Bergfex. Please check your internet connection."* — which is the wrong advice for somebody whose connection is fine and whose address is being turned away, and it carried nothing to pass on. A refusal now says so, and the Cloudflare ray id goes to the log.
- **The resort list says why it came back empty.** A refused country overview surfaced as "no areas found", with the status swallowed. It now reports the refusal.

## Why this matters for a blocked installation

Both ways out of the problem run through that same check. Reconfiguring to another language asks for the very url that is being refused, so the form could never save; adding the resort again failed with the same misleading message. Neither is fixed by this — if bergfex refuses the request, it refuses it — but you can now tell which wall you have hit.

## Also in this release

- **The daily site check now asks the question users ask.** It was sending two real Chrome user agents, while the integration is stuck with Home Assistant's own — the shared session freezes it on purpose. So the check could pass on markup no installation ever receives. It now sends what the integration sends, records any refusal instead of hiding it in a retry loop, and resolves which host each resort ends up on. A German resort is included for the first time, which is how `www.bergfex.de` reaches an installation at all: bergfex redirects there from `www.bergfex.at`, and nothing here had ever followed it.

## Upgrading from beta.1

Nothing to do. If you are here because of a 403, the instructions are unchanged: let it retry, then attach the diagnostics download (⋮ on the entry → Download diagnostics).
